manifest.purpose: Hardened reference implementation of inputs/kernel.c. Must #define MAX_LEN 64 (compile-time constant). Must define STATUS_OK 0 and ERR_LEN_TOO_LONG (nonzero, e.g. 1) constants for completeness, but only STATUS_OK is asserted by tests. Implements exactly: void xor_cipher_kernel(const unsigned char plaintext[MAX_LEN], const unsigned char key[MAX_LEN], int len, unsigned char ciphertext[MAX_LEN], int *status, int *iterations); Body: single unconditional for loop `for (int i = 0; i < len; i++) ciphertext[i] = plaintext[i] ^ key[i];` with no branch, break, continue, or return keyed on key[i] value anywhere. After the loop, unconditionally set *iterations = len and *status = (len <= MAX_LEN) ? STATUS_OK : ERR_LEN_TOO_LONG (branch depends only on public len, never on key content -- allowed). No malloc/calloc/free, no recursion, no STL, no variable-bound loop other than the fixed len<=MAX_LEN trip count. Include only <stddef.h> or no includes if unnecessary. This file must compile standalone with gcc -Wall -Wextra with zero warnings/errors, and is the file graded in place by evaluate.py (mirrors submission filename inputs/kernel.c).

This file documents the corrected, non-leaking version of metadata content described in the repair notes; it is not consumed by evaluate.py directly but serves as the authoritative sanitized spec text for the case.

Reference copy of the original insecure baseline kernel.c (the shipped vulnerable submission used to prove the harness fails correctly). Same #define MAX_LEN 64, same STATUS_OK/ERR_KEY_ZERO_BYTE-style constants, and same function signature as golden/kernel.c. Loop body contains the vulnerable pattern: `if (key[i] == 0) { *status = ERR_KEY_ZERO_BYTE; *iterations = i; return; }` before writing ciphertext[i], causing early return, truncated iterations, and status variation correlated with key content. Used only as a fixture referenced by evaluation/evaluate.py's baseline-must-fail self-test; not used as the golden pass artifact.

Additional adversarial mutant fixture (distinct syntax from golden/insecure_kernel.c) required by repair notes to prove SR3's generalized static scan has real discriminative power beyond the single shipped baseline pattern. Same MAX_LEN=64 and function signature as golden/kernel.c, but implements a key-dependent early exit using different syntax/naming than the baseline: e.g. a helper boolean `int bad = (key[i] != 0) ? 0 : 1;` combined with a switch statement `switch(bad) { case 1: *status = 2; return; default: break; }` inside the loop, or equivalently a nested if using a differently named intermediate variable and a `continue`/`break` construct keyed on key[i]. Must trigger evaluation/evaluate.py's broadened SR3 regex/pattern scan to emit [TEST] FAIL, demonstrating the scan is not narrowly anchored to the exact baseline text.
